quiz: REST URLs name things (nouns), and the HTTP method says the action. Avoid verbs inside the path.
Idempotent means sending the same request many times has the same effect as once. Which method creates a new thing each time?
The key exists to make retries safe. If the first attempt already finished, what should a retry get back?
Same key but a different body is a client mistake. Silently replaying or processing both would hide the bug.
In merge patch, null means remove the field and nested objects are merged, not replaced. Apply that rule step by step.
To hide whether an item exists, the response for someone else's item should look the same as for a missing item.
The JSON is well-formed, so syntax is fine. Which code is more precise for values that break business rules?
Think about how the database finds page N with an offset versus jumping straight to a remembered position using an index.
If many rows share the same sort value, the cursor is ambiguous. What makes each row's position unique?
A breaking change makes old clients fail. Which change rejects requests that used to work?
The name is misleading. Ask whether the cache may keep the response, and what it must do before reusing it.
The cache asks the origin if its copy is still current, sending its tag. What does the origin send when nothing changed?
If-Match is a precondition on writes. What status means the precondition did not hold?
Links tell the client what it can do next. Who then decides which actions are valid in the current state?
interview: Start from the domain nouns, use plural collections and ids, nest only for real ownership, and let methods carry the verbs.
Define safe and idempotent separately, then classify each method and explain why POST and some PATCH are not idempotent.
Explain client-generated idempotency keys, storing the result, replaying it, rejecting key reuse with a different body.
Contrast full replacement with partial updates, and mention missing fields, idempotency, and patch formats.
Explain how null deletes and objects merge, then note it cannot set a value to null or edit arrays item by item.
Give the meaning of each code, using bad syntax, missing login, no permission, not found, conflict, and invalid values.
Compare simplicity and jump-to-page with speed and stability under inserts, and say which fits which UI.
Mention allow-listing sort fields, parameter binding for filters, limits on page size, and indexes for common sorts.
Cover URL or header versioning, additive changes, deprecation, and what changes break existing clients.
Define links in responses that show allowed actions, then give an honest view of when it is worth it.
Mention contract-first design, generated docs, client and server code generation, and contract tests in CI.
Explain caching directives like max-age and no-cache, then how a client revalidates with a tag and gets 304.
Explain If-Match on writes, rejecting with 412 if the tag changed, and 428 when the precondition is required.
Describe returning 202 with a job resource, polling or callbacks, status states, and fetching the result when done.
